chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Mad'ani, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said:
"Any child of fornication born in the Time of Ignorance belongs to the one who claims him from among the people of Islam."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The ruling I act upon and issue fatwa based on is what these narrations contain, that the child of fornication does not inherit and his parents do not inherit from him, nor do those related to them, and his inheritance goes to the one who guarantees his sin or to the Imam of the Muslims, because inheritance is only established through correct lineages in Islamic law, and the child of fornication has no correct lineage.
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rules for a child of fornication in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration clarifies that the 'child of fornication' lacks a valid legal lineage (*nasab*) for inheritance purposes, meaning he neither inherits from nor is inherited by his parents. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan emphasizes that his estate reverts to the one who guarantees his sin or to the Imam, reflecting the Shia juristic view that inheritance is strictly tied to recognized kinship. This ruling underscores the distinction between biological paternity and legal inheritance rights in cases of illicit union.
